what_its_for: Latanoprost is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is used to treat a condition called glaucoma and high eye pressure (ocular hypertension). Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve.
how_to_take: Use latanoprost eye drops exactly as your doctor tells you. Wash your hands thoroughly before using. Tilt your head back, gently pull your lower eyelid down to form a small pocket, and place one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press your finger lightly against the inner corner of your eye (near your nose). This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces the chance of side effects. Do not touch the tip of the dropper to your eye, eyelid, or any other surface to avoid contamination. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each different eye medication.
dosing: The usual dose is ONE drop in the affected eye or eyes ONCE a day in the EVENING. Use it at the same time each evening to help you remember. Do not use more than one drop per day, as using it more often can actually make it work less well.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and use your next drop the following evening at your regular time. Do not use two drops to make up for the one you missed. Just continue with your normal schedule.
storage: Before opening: Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). After opening: You may store the open bottle at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Throw away any opened bottle after 6 weeks, even if there is medicine left in it. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine away from light, heat, and out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the tip of the dropper to your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep the drops from getting contaminated. Do not use the drops while wearing contact lenses — wait 15 minutes after using the drops before inserting your lenses. Avoid driving or using machinery right after using the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry. Do not use more drops than prescribed, as this will not lower eye pressure more and may cause problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: sudden vision changes or loss of vision, eye pain or increased eye redness, signs of an eye infection (discharge, swelling, or increased sensitivity to light), swelling of your eyelids or the area around your eye, chest pain or difficulty breathing, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as severe rash, itching, or swelling of the face or throat. Also let your doctor know if you notice changes in your eye color (the iris may gradually turn more brown), increased growth or darkening of your eyelashes, or darkening of the skin around your eyes, as these can be long-term side effects.
when_it_works: Latanoprost starts to lower eye pressure within 3 to 4 hours after using it. It reaches its best effect at around 8 to 12 hours. You likely will not feel it working since high eye pressure usually has no symptoms. Your doctor will check your eye pressure during follow-up visits to make sure the medicine is working properly. It is important to keep using the drops every day even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of latanoprost during pregnancy has not been fully established, so your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks with you. Children: Latanoprost can be used in children but only under the close guidance of a doctor. Older adults: No special dose changes are usually needed for older adults, but let your doctor know of all other medications you are taking. People with certain eye conditions: Tell your doctor if you have had eye surgery, a history of inflammation in the eye (uveitis or iritis), or if you only have one working eye, as extra caution may be needed.
